chunks: And Safwān narrated from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “A slaughtered bird was gifted to us in Makkah, and our family ate it.” So he said: “The people of Makkah do not regard any harm in it.” I said: “Then what do you say, you?” He said: “Its price is upon them.”
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a hunted bird in Makkah is gifted to someone and then eaten?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slaughtered bird gifted in Makkah and eaten by the family. Although the people of Makkah saw no problem in it, Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام ruled that compensation in the form of its price was due. The report relates to the rulings of hunting and liability within the Sanctuary.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2364 - Safwan narrated from Mansur ibn Hazim:

I said to Abu Abdullah (as), "A slaughtered bird was gifted to us in Mecca, and our family ate it."
Imam (as) replied: "The people of Mecca see no harm in it."
I asked: "What do you say about it?"
Imam (as) said: "They are liable for its price."
